extracted.intended_audience: research authors preparing manuscripts for journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on drafting a Data Availability Statement (DAS) for journal manuscript submission, including wording templates, placement, repository/linking options, and reasons when data cannot be shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Data Availability Statement (DAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Data Availability Statement (also called Data Access Statement) tells the reader if the data behind a research project can be accessed and, if so, where and how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear information about accessibility and access routes; when possible include hyperlinks to public databases to make it easier for readers to find the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of the DAS in the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: A DAS is normally included in a very visible place in the manuscript right before the reference section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a journal provides specific placement instructions follow them; otherwise place the DAS immediately before the references so readers can find it easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide permanent web links for shared data
rubrics_metrics.description: The most common practice to share datasets is to provide a permanent web link. This way, almost universal access is guaranteed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include persistent identifiers or permanent URLs (e.g., DOI or stable repository links). Where possible hyperlink directly to the dataset to ease reuse and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify which data are available (raw vs processed)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether raw and/or processed data required to reproduce the findings are available and provide links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit template phrasing such as: 'The raw data required to reproduce the above findings are available to download from [INSERT PERMANENT WEB LINK(s)]. The processed data required to reproduce the above findings are available to download from [INSERT PERMANENT WEB LINK(s)].'

rubrics_metrics.name: If data are not available, state the reason
rubrics_metrics.description: When data cannot be shared, the DAS should explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example phrasings provided: 'The raw/processed data required to reproduce the above findings cannot be shared at this time due to legal/ ethical reasons.'; '... due to technical/ time limitations.'; '... as the data also forms part of an ongoing study.' Be specific about the restriction (legal, ethical, technical, ongoing study, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the DAS concise (one or two sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: DAS’ are normally only one or two sentences, so there is really no reason why it shouldn’t be included in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be succinct while providing the essential information: accessibility, location (link), and any restriction reason. Use journal templates if available to stay concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow journal- or funder-specific policies and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are currently in the process of submitting an article to a journal, you should check its guidelines and policy; most journals offer templates for different kinds of DAS formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When specific journal instructions are present, use those templates or wording. If absent, adapt the example templates supplied and replace bracketed information. Also check funder requirements for data sharing and statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository choice and linking options
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no restrictions concerning the choice of a database; authors can use whatever database they want, though a journal may invite upload to a specific one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an appropriate repository (discipline-specific or general-purpose) and provide permanent links; you may also link your dataset directly to your article if supported by the journal. Follow any repository recommendations by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAS supports reproducibility and data validation
rubrics_metrics.description: A DAS should provide the necessary information for others to reproduce works stated or reported in an article, supporting data validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enough detail (what data, where, and how to access) so readers can validate the quality and legitimacy of the underlying data. Making data accessible enables checking and verification of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAS promotes reuse and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Availability Statements allow research data to be easily found and properly examined and validated by scientists who might need it for further research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links and repository details that enable indexing and discovery (e.g., repository metadata, DOIs) to facilitate reuse and incorporation into future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAS enables proper citation and author recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Including a DAS helps improve the chances of being (properly) cited by other researchers and contributes to author recognition (e.g., linking to datasets that can be cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible provide citation information for datasets (DOI, citation text) so others can cite the data properly, supporting credit (e.g., h-index relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions: reviews without original data may not need a DAS
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of research reviews that are not based on original data, such a statement is not needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether your article uses original data; for literature reviews with no underlying data generation, state that the manuscript does not include new data if that aligns with journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the publisher's submission tools for DAS when available
rubrics_metrics.description: The majority of Elsevier journals will have integrated the option to create a Data Availability Statement directly in the submission flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting, use the submission system prompts to complete the DAS; the system will guide the steps and ensure placement and conformity with journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor example templates to fit your needs
rubrics_metrics.description: When specific journal instructions regarding how to formulate a DAS are absent or unavailable, consider tailoring or combining example templates to fit your needs (replace bracketed information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize provided example sentences to accurately reflect your data sharing situation, ensuring clarity and truthfulness while keeping concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAS contributes to transparency, compliance, and trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits for authors and readers include increases transparency, allows compliance with data policies, and encourages good scientific practice and trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame your DAS to align with these aims: be transparent about data availability, comply with journal/funder rules, and promote trustworthy reporting by providing access details or justified restrictions.
